fields.title: inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.statement: As an engineer reviewing decomposition, I want to see the other items contributing under the relevant parent so I can judge the family together rather than inspect isolated statements.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** the parent and relationship defining the family are explainable; shared children remain recognizable as the same underlying item; editing one identity does not create divergence among its appearances; users can return to the wider scope with drafts intact.
fields.exceptions: **Exceptions:** a child belongs to two parents, appears along several paths, or has different kinds of sibling relationships. Test whether the user wants immediate siblings or the whole branch; do not assume they are equivalent.

fields.title: resolve one meaningful completeness gap
fields.statement: As an engineer building a design, I want to know which obligation is unresolved and why so I can choose the next appropriate work.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance:
**Candidate acceptance:** a displayed gap has an explainable expectation and scope; the user can inspect existing candidates before creating duplicate information; an appropriate new connection resolves that structural gap without falsely declaring the design/evidence valid; other unresolved obligations remain visible.

**Software acceptance example (UR-15):** where the project marks a requirement approved, see whether an actual implementation artifact is linked. With no such link, show implementation as not traced and likely outstanding; offer the task choices of implementing it, linking existing code or investigating uncertainty. Do not force a new implementation when the code already exists. A link to a planned task/design is not an actual-code realization link; partial or outdated mappings retain their unresolved scope. Adding an appropriate link closes the trace gap, not automatically the implementation/verification judgment.
fields.exceptions: **Exceptions:** an item is intentionally not applicable, the expectation is unknown, existing implementation is unlinked, a link covers only part of the requirement or refers to older behavior, or old evidence uses different inputs. Represent uncertainty rather than inventing a complete/incomplete judgment.

fields.title: quantitative meaning without overconstraint
fields.statement: As an engineer changing an important specification, I want to understand where the value comes from and where it is used so I can assess the consequences without forcing every requirement into a formal model.
fields.sourceHeading: ## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance examples:**

fields.title: begin without an extensive setup detour
fields.statement: As an author starting a design, I want to work with recognizable information so I can begin expressing the design instead of learning the tool's internal model.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** users recognize the available information and what is missing; they can start one meaningful item without first constructing a complete project ontology. Existing data brought into the project is not silently lost or falsely represented as validated.
fields.exceptions: **Investigate:** write from scratch, paste/import or start from a template? Prototype these alternatives rather than implementing all three now.

fields.title: reassess evidence without rewriting its past
fields.statement: As a reviewer, I want to inspect changed inputs and the original evidence so I can record why the evidence does or does not support the decision now.
fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** coverage, freshness, uncertainty and review decision remain separate; original snapshots/rationale remain accessible; the comparison used while drafting is identifiable; a relevant intervening change requires an explicit new assessment rather than silent token adoption; acceptance does not erase drift.
fields.exceptions: **Exceptions:** missing observations, unrelated edits, relevant later changes, superseded evidence and conflicting reviewer assumptions. Local provenance labels are not authenticated approval authority.

fields.title: resume and recover safely
fields.statement: As an engineer interrupted during work, I want to retain my proposal and orientation so I can resume or reconcile it without losing information or overwriting someone else's change.
fields.sourceHeading: ## 5. Cross-cutting story R-01 — resume and recover safely
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** context/selection and save status are understandable; switching level or representation does not silently discard drafts; a failed read cannot authorize editing stale information as if current; object/schema conflicts preserve the attempt; historical inspection does not masquerade as editing current state.
fields.exceptions: **Investigate:** autosave versus explicit save, reopening after shutdown, undo, and what should be retained across sessions. Prototype and actual repository safety capabilities may differ; label unsupported recovery behavior honestly.

fields.title: see impact before accepting a change
fields.statement: As an engineer proposing a modification, I want to compare it with the established state and inspect explainable consequences so I can review the proposal before changing the authoritative design.
fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** proposed versus committed information is distinguishable; impact candidates show the paths/reasons that make them relevant; browsing does not write changes; connection alone is not presented as proof that the connected item must change; unmodeled consequences remain explicitly possible.
fields.exceptions: **Exceptions:** cyclic or dense networks, shared children, changed schema, missing/deleted items and incomplete source knowledge. A bounded result must explain its scope, not imply a complete impact census.

fields.title: author in context and move between levels
fields.statement: As an author, I want to inspect the relevant parent intent while writing a child requirement so I can explain how the child contributes without repeatedly reconstructing context.
fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** free text is usable without compulsory formal syntax; an item can relate to an existing parent or remain explicitly unlinked; applicable field/relationship actions are reachable in the working context; changing scope does not silently lose the draft.
fields.exceptions: **Exceptions:** long statements, optional attributes, multiple parents, uncertain relationships and a parent that changed while drafting.

fields.title: reason about removal
fields.statement: As an engineer considering removing information, I want to see what relies on it so I can decide how to address those obligations without losing the established history.
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.acceptance: **Candidate acceptance:** removing, filtering out, disconnecting and superseding are distinguishable; references and unresolved obligations are explained; no silent cascade; established history remains inspectable; users know whether anything was committed.
fields.exceptions: **Investigate:** actual review/approval authority and the semantics of retirement versus deletion. Do not introduce automatic cascade or organizational approval merely because it would simplify a mockup.
